details:
A lot of avatars don't have realistic proportions, as such, by stretching the arms IRL it is possible to reach farther than the avatar can. I propose a way to automatically scale the arm bones (on the local axis) to mitigate this problem.
Some people prefer the look of taller legs and shorter arms, this is why I request 2 different systems, to account for both cases:
- System #1 (Passive) - Avatars are scaled as they are in the present, however, if the user is able to reach farther than the avatar at some angles the arm bones are stretched to accommodate for the user being able to do so temporarily.
- System #2 (Toggle) - A new option is created called "Realistic Avatar Proportions" which modifies the avatar's arm-span to make them realistically proportionate to the avatar's height, similar to human proportions. This is for those that don't mind changing an avatar's proportions to match their own, eliminating floor-level mismatch.
The first system can be used simultaneously with the second one (in case the shoulders are weirdly positioned).
Arguments against:
- Human bones don't stretch IRL, it would be weird to do that in-game.
Yes, they don't. However, the arms only need to be scaled by a small percentage and still make a huge difference in terms of proportions. At this scale it is not noticeable, way less than the avatar not being able to stretch its arms forward to match your controller's position.
- I like the look of my avatar, I don't want to change the proportions.
This is why I proposed both systems. One as a toggle that changes the avatar proportions to realistic ones and another one that just passively accommodates with less effect.
Possible implementations:
- The bones need to be scaled along the local axis and not moved. By moving the wrist bones it messes with avatars that have separate meshes(ex: robotic joints, etc) Properly stretching the arm bones instead of moving them fixes this problem.
title: [FEEDBACK] Option to scale arm bones to combat bad proportions
